subject: physiology
title: Forced expiration and flow-volume interpretation
description: Forced expiration depends on lung volume, airway tethering and the pressure that also compresses the airways. Interpreting a forced tracing requires both the volume exhaled and how quickly it leaves.

subject: physiology
title: Oxygenation, ventilation and cellular oxygen use
description: A low tissue oxygen supply can arise from different levels of the respiratory pathway. Changes in inspired oxygen have different consequences when the limiting step is ventilation, diffusion, blood transport or cellular use.

subject: physiology
title: Alveolar collapse, fibrosis and pulmonary vascular loss
description: Respiratory disease may change the airways, exchange surface and pulmonary vascular bed simultaneously. The consequences depend on whether lung units lose ventilation, perfusion, structural support or the capacity to expand.

subject: physiology
title: Assisted ventilation and competing respiratory pressures
description: Assisted ventilation changes the pressure that moves air and may also change cardiovascular filling. The signs of pressure and the measurement conditions must be explicit before comparing spontaneous and assisted breaths.

subject: physiology
title: Compliance, surface tension and pressure-volume history
description: Lung mechanics depend on tissue elasticity, the alveolar surface film and whether a measurement is taken during inflation or deflation. Models are most useful when their assumptions are stated.

subject: physiology
title: Effective ventilation under changing dead space
description: Minute ventilation must be separated into dead-space and alveolar ventilation. The effect on CO2 also depends on metabolic production, so normal breathing frequency or total minute volume alone is insufficient.

subject: physiology
title: Regional blood flow and edema forces
description: Pulmonary flow depends on the relationship between alveolar, arterial and venous pressures. Fluid movement depends on a separate balance of hydrostatic and oncotic forces, modified by lymphatic removal.

subject: physiology
title: Regional matching and venous admixture
description: The distribution of ventilation and perfusion matters as much as their total values. Mixing must be performed using oxygen content and blood-flow fractions before inferring a mixed oxygen pressure.

subject: physiology
title: Oxygen carriage, delivery and unloading
description: Arterial PO2, hemoglobin saturation, content and delivery describe different quantities. Applying oxygen transport requires tracking bound oxygen, flow and tissue extraction separately.

subject: physiology
title: Chemical respiratory control across time and sites
description: Central and peripheral respiratory feedback differ in stimulus and response timing. Blood oxygen content and oxygen tension must also be distinguished when interpreting the peripheral response.

subject: anatomy
title: Nasal neurovascular pathways and injury localization
description: Nasal symptoms localize differently when a lesion affects trigeminal sensory branches, olfactory axons or autonomic fibers. Arterial pathways also explain why bleeding and surgical injury can extend beyond the visible nasal cavity.

subject: anatomy
title: Laryngeal tissue mechanics and routes of spread
description: Vocal-fold immobility can reflect invasion of muscle or nearby spaces as well as nerve injury. Superficial tissue edema, nodules and obstruction of glandular outflow alter voice or airway function by different anatomical mechanisms.

subject: anatomy
title: Pleural compartments and procedural boundaries
description: The pleural sacs extend into regions that are easy to overlook when reasoning only from the visible lung border. Their closed compartments and extrapleural planes explain why an injury may spare the opposite lung or enter the pleura from a neck or flank approach.

subject: anatomy
title: Shared pulmonary drainage and hilar relationships
description: Bronchi and pulmonary arteries organize segmental supply, while pulmonary veins often drain shared boundaries and combine territories. Hilar orientation and variant systemic supply add information that a bronchial label alone cannot provide.

subject: histology
title: Epithelial defense, sensory pathways and small-airway injury
description: Respiratory defense combines particle capture, ciliary movement and secretory support with distinct sensory and renewal pathways. Comparing preserved functions with lost ones also separates bronchiolar muscle tone from fixed wall remodeling.

subject: histology
title: Alveolar barrier, surfactant and repair
description: Alveolar function requires a thin sealed interface, preserved septal area and a surface film supported by viable epithelial cells. Type II-cell repair and macrophage clearance add functions that cannot be inferred from oxygen diffusion or surfactant mechanics alone.

subject: embryology
title: Localizing airway-development and maturation defects
description: Airway induction, foregut partitioning, laryngeal recanalization and distal exchange maturation are distinct processes. A preserved early structure narrows the defect but does not establish that later branching or the blood-air interface has matured.
